---
title: "Pipelines"
---

Four sources feed the analysis. Each one is joined to the others on census tract.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  acs[ACS income and population] --> profiles[Tract profiles]
  housing[Housing inventory] --> projects[Project rows]
  services[Services and supportive housing] --> rates[Rates per 1,000]
  calls[311 requests] --> need[Request counts]
  profiles --> ami[Affordability comparison]
  projects --> ami
  rates --> ssi[Saturation index]
  need --> ssi
```

## Census income and population

The tract file is the Census Bureau's 2023 American Community Survey 5-year tables, limited to the tracts New York City Planning assigns to community-district tabulation area MN09. With `CENSUS_API_KEY` set, the script uses the Census API. Without a key, it reads the Bureau's 2023 5-year summary files and keeps those same tables.

| Variable | Table | Universe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median household income, and its margin of error | B19013 | Households |
| Poverty count and poverty universe | B17001 | Population for whom poverty status is determined |
| Median gross rent, and its margin of error | B25064 | Renter-occupied units paying cash rent |
| Total population, and its margin of error | B01003 | Total population |

Vintage and universe are stored on every row. The snapshot stays in `data/retrieved/`.

## Housing production

HPD's Affordable Housing Production by Building dataset (`hg8x-zxpr`) is the building file for community board MN-09. A project enters the unit total only when that file has the building. HPD's counted units are the agency's affordable-unit field. They are not reclassified into AMI bands. 1727 Amsterdam is recorded from the borough president's recommendation and is kept out of the sum, because the unit count there is approximate.

## Services and supportive housing

The saturation index uses three rates per 1,000 residents: mental-health and behavioral-health sites, permanent supportive housing units, and food pantries. The formula is on the saturation page. There is no public site list for those facilities in this repository, so the index is not scored.

## 311 requests

The extract asks NYC Open Data (`erm2-nwe9`) for complaint-type counts in community board `09 MANHATTAN` during calendar years 2023 and 2024. The aggregation runs on the open-data server. The table keeps two types the complaint-type field actually uses: Homeless Person Assistance and Encampment. Bus-stop shelter complaints are left out. The counts are community-board totals, not a tract split.

## What each pipeline supplies

| Pipeline | What the analysis uses |
| --- | --- |
| Census income | 2023 five-year medians, poverty, rent, and population for the 20 MN09 tracts |
| Housing inventory | Two HPD buildings in the unit total, and 1727 Amsterdam listed separately |
| Services | The weighted saturation formula, with no score |
| 311 counts | Homeless Person Assistance and Encampment, by year |
